naslov: Whoever Gives Something Up for Allah's Sake, Allah Will Replace It with Something Better

segmenti.tekst: [Arabic recitation]

لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين، صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وأصحابه الكرام الهداة المهتدين وسلم تسليما كثيرا إلى يوم الدين. قال الله في كتابه الكريم: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ. Praise belongs to the One, Exalted Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), Lord of all the worlds, Lord of the Day of Judgment,

Lord of jinn and mankind. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Dear brothers, respected congregation, when Suhayb ar-Rumi, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, decided

to make the hijrah (emigration) – Suhayb, who as a child was abducted by the Romans and then sold to the Quraysh; Suhayb, who grew up with them, or among them, as a slave, and as such managed to gather a lot of money.
As such he managed to gather a lot of money, which he hid, buried in a place no one knew.

Suhayb, who was one of the first to accept Islam; Suhayb, who set out to make the hijrah, but the Quraysh did not allow him; then he set out to make the hijrah in secret, without anyone's knowledge, but the Quraysh heard about it and went after him.

And they caught up with him on a hill between Mecca and Medina. And they surrounded him. There Suhayb ar-Rumi addressed them with the words: “O Quraysh, O Quraysh, you know that I am the best archer among you.
I have about twenty arrows with me. Whoever comes at me, I will kill him.” He said: “What good would it do you for about twenty of your men to be killed?
You need nothing of it. Better let me go, and I will give you something in return.” And the Quraysh accepted that. Suhayb said to them: “At such and such a place you have so many gold coins buried.

At such and such a place you have so many dirhams buried. With such and such a man you have so many camels, so many sheep. Go and take it all.” That is, Suhayb gave everything in order to gain the pleasure of Allah.

After that Suhayb, radiyallahu ta'ala anhu (may Allah be pleased with him), arrived in Medina. At the entrance to Medina the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was waiting for him with the words: “Rabiha al-bay'u, ya Aba Yahya” – your trade has succeeded, O Abu Yahya, your trade has succeeded, O Abu Suhayb. After that Allah [unclear] and revealed verses to the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam: “Wa min an-nasi man yashri nafsahu ibtigha'a mardatillah.”
And there are people who sacrifice themselves for the sake of Allah's pleasure. They sacrifice themselves for the sake of Allah's pleasure. My dear brothers, trade with Allah is the best trade.

The example of Suhayb is an example of how a person, a Muslim, should sacrifice himself for the sake of Allah's pleasure. And whoever sacrifices himself for the sake of Allah's pleasure, Allah will give him better and more than what he left for the sake of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.
These are the words of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam: that whoever leaves something for the sake of Allah, Allah will give him something better than it.
My dear brothers, whoever works in a place where [unclear] the boss does not allow him to attend Jumu'ah – does not allow him to perform the prayer – let him leave that place for the sake of Allah.
Allah will give him better than that. If someone works in a place where other people's rights, other people's money, are taken unjustly, let him leave that place.
Allah will give him better than that. If someone works in a place where haram is served, let him leave that place. Allah will give him better than that. This is not my promise.
This is the promise of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: “وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا” – and whoever fears Allah, Allah will make for him a way out.

“وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ” – and will provide for him from where he does not expect. What a beautiful promise of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala! The most beautiful example of this, my brothers, is the example of Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam, who was thrown into a well as a child, then they found him and sold him to a rich man in Egypt,
a minister, in whose house Yusuf grew up, grew up into the most handsome young man.
This Aziz, or this man, the sayyid (master), the rich man, had a beautiful wife, who fell in love with Yusuf, who asked him to commit zina (fornication) with her.
Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam, refused, even though it cost him a lot, even though it cost him prison, being in prison, only because he did not want to commit zina with her.

What does Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam, say? “Rabbi as-sijnu ahabbu ilayya mimma yad'unani ilayh.” He said: “My Lord, prison is the better option for me. I prefer prison to doing what this woman invites me to.” What happens to Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam, after that?
Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam, says – it is mentioned in the Qur'an:
[Arabic recitation]

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, gave Yusuf authority. Authority, executive authority. He could do whatever he wanted. That is the reward. And the reward of Suhayb, my dear brothers, is that he became the best merchant, that he was one of the best merchants in Medina and the richest man.

This Suhayb, whom we mentioned at the beginning – that is the reward. The reward of the one who trades with Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. It is stated in the narrations that a certain caliph had many slave women and slaves. However, among the slaves and slave women he had one beautiful slave girl who was pious.
And, it is said, whenever that slave girl passed by, a young man would look at her. That bothered her, and she went to the caliph to complain. She said: “So-and-so looks at me.”

The caliph said to her: “Put on your most beautiful clothes and go to him.” And he ordered, ordered the chief of his police that, if this young man stretched out his hand toward this girl, they should cut off his hand and kill him.

When this girl went to the door of this young man, he opened the door and immediately understood what she wanted from him. So he raised his hands toward the heavens, saying: “My Lord, is this how You test Your servants?
My Lord, is this how You test Your servants?” And he closed the door. What was the reward, dear brothers? The reward was that the caliph freed him from slavery and married him to this slave girl.

That is the reward. That is the reward for the one who fears Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Also, dear brothers, the one who is in a position to take revenge on his brother, his children, his wife at a given moment, Allah promises him a great reward.

The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: “Man kazama ghayzan wa huwa qadirun 'ala an yunfidhahu” – whoever restrains his anger while he is able to act on it, to take revenge – “da'ahullahu yawm al-qiyamati 'ala ru'us al-khala'iq” – he said, Allah will place him on the Day of Judgment at the head of His creatures – “hatta yukhayyirahu min ayyi al-hur al-'in ma sha'” – and, he said, He will let him choose as many houris as he wishes.

As many houris as he wishes. All of us, dear brothers, are sometimes in a position to take revenge on a Muslim brother, on our children for disobedience, on our wife, and so on. But whoever suppresses his anger and is merciful, Allah promises him this great reward.

Not only does Allah promise him a reward, dear brothers, but also that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will protect him from misfortunes, evil, illness, and so on. That is the promise of our Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, to whom revelation was sent down from Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

And that is why every person, every mu'min, every Muslim must and should trade with Allah, so that he may succeed in this world and, by Allah, in the Hereafter too. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among those who fear only Him. I ask Him, the Exalted, to forgive us our sins and the sins of our parents. I ask Him, the Exalted, to unite us in Jannah (Paradise). Amin, ya Rabb al-alamin. Aqulu qawli hadha wa astaghfirullaha li wa lakum,
فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
